definitions.gloss: food simmered in sweetened soy sauce or sugar syrup; sweet-simmered
definitions.explanation: A Japanese cooking method where ingredients are slowly simmered in a sweet mixture of sugar, soy sauce, and mirin until glazed and tender. Common with small fish, chestnuts, and other ingredients.

examples.japanese: {鮎|あゆ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{甘露煮|かんろに}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made sweetfish simmered in sweet soy.

examples.english: Sweet-simmered chestnuts are a staple of New Year's dishes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦{小魚|こざかな}→小魚：28694_kozakana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{甘露煮|かんろに}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{骨|ほね}→骨：02166_hone⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{柔|やわ}らかくて→柔らかい：01096_yawarakai⟧⟦{絶品|ぜっぴん}→絶品：13811_zeppin⟧だった。
examples.english: The sweet-simmered small fish my grandmother made were exquisite — tender right through to the bones.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{甘露|かんろ}→甘露：21361_kanro⟧ (sweet nectar) and ⟦{煮|に}→煮る：01971_niru⟧ (simmering/cooking). A traditional Japanese preservation and cooking technique. The long, slow simmering in sweetened liquid gives the food a glossy, caramelized appearance and a sweet-savory flavor. Particularly associated with {鮎|あゆ} (sweetfish), ⟦{栗|くり}→栗：04387_kuri⟧ (chestnuts), and ⟦{佃煮|つくだに}→佃煮：04970_tsukudani⟧-style small fish.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鮎|あゆ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{甘露煮|かんろに}: candied sweetfish
- ⟦{栗|くり}→栗：04387_kuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{甘露煮|かんろに}: candied chestnuts
- {甘露煮|かんろに}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to simmer in sweet syrup

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{佃煮|つくだに}→佃煮：04970_tsukudani⟧: food simmered in soy and sugar — similar but typically uses stronger soy flavor and smaller pieces
- ⟦{煮付|につ}け→煮付け：18831_nitsuke⟧: food simmered in seasoned broth — broader category, not necessarily sweet
- {砂糖漬|さとうづ}け: preserved in sugar — uses sugar without cooking
